source_review.notes: Checked all six references at the RFC Editor or official AWS documentation. RFC 9421 confirms selected HTTP component signatures, created/expires/nonce/keyid/tag parameters, application-profile obligations, and replay risks from incomplete coverage. RFC 9530 confirms Content-Digest versus Repr-Digest semantics. RFC 9449 confirms DPoP jti/htm/htu/iat/ath/nonce and replay-ledger limitations. RFC 2104 supplies the HMAC construction; RFC 9110 supplies current HTTP semantics. AWS SigV4 documents canonical request, signed headers, payload hash, credential scope, and time-bound signing as a mature profile example.

evidence: Reviewed request r, proof p, key record k, signature base B(r,p), validation predicates, replay key tuple, retention inequality, and allow predicate for consistent definitions.
Confirmed proof verification, TLS, authorization, and business invariant symbols are distinct and all TeX uses GitHub-compatible delimiters.
Confirmed replay-safe proof, idempotent execution, sender-constrained token, nonce/JTI, and content/representation digest terminology is scoped precisely.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation makes the central non-substitution rule visible: valid selected-component proof is only one conjunct of an allowed, nonduplicated business operation.

evidence: Recomputed the executable time boundary: NOW-(NOW-10)=10 is within MAX_AGE=120, while NOW-(NOW-121)=121 is rejected.
Checked future allowance is at most five model seconds and replay retention prose requires coverage through the final skewed acceptance.
Verified the RFC 2104 SHA-256 HMAC block size used by the model is 64 bytes and the padding constants are 0x36 and 0x5c.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The model's fixed times and key are deterministic test inputs, not production recommendations for age, skew, key material, or nonce entropy.

evidence: Expanded V_proof into key, algorithm, signature-base, time, nonce, context, and content predicates; removing any conjunct recreates a documented relocation, tampering, stale, or replay case.
Re-derived allow as TLS AND proof AND authorization AND domain invariant, confirming signatures do not imply confidentiality or permission.
Checked the retention condition t_retain >= t_last-accept and scoped atomic uniqueness are sufficient to prevent a second acceptance of the same nonce under the stated complete-ledger assumptions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The argument is explicitly conditional on primitive security, key custody, canonicalization/profile completeness, and ledger coverage.

evidence: Reviewed unsigned/altered method, authority, path, query duplicates/encoding/order, fields, tenant/idempotency data, content/digest/content type, signature metadata, token, redirect, and proxy rewrite cases.

Reviewed exact replay, concurrent cross-node/region replay, per-process caches, check/insert races, early expiry, clock past/future/skew, challenge/pre-generation, huge nonce/ledger exhaustion, partitions/outage, and fail-open behavior.

Reviewed raw/parsed JSON, duplicates/Unicode/numbers, content/transfer encoding, streaming/trailers, DPoP body/query limits, HMAC/asymmetric algorithm confusion, key rotation/revocation, presigned URL leakage, legitimate retries, fresh duplicate commands, webhooks, and unsafe logs/errors.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial review covers cryptographic coverage, HTTP ambiguity, distributed uniqueness, resource exhaustion, credential lifecycle, and domain duplication.

evidence: Executed signed-request-replay-model: first request allowed; exact duplicate denied by nonce state; body tampering and target relocation denied by signature; 121-second proof denied by time.
Checked the hand-coded educational RFC 2104 construction against the inner/outer padded SHA-256 form and comparison scans all equal-length bytes without content-dependent early return.

Checked signed-component completeness, authenticate-before-ledger-insert, atomic uniqueness, fresh-proof/stable-idempotency retry, key-policy binding, and authorization-after-proof invariants across examples and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: The one-process model cannot establish RFC 9421 interoperability, production cryptographic implementation safety, proxy behavior, distributed atomicity, or business execution semantics.

proof_review.notes: No formal reduction for signature/HMAC unforgeability, canonicalization equivalence, distributed linearizability, sender constraint, authorization, or exactly-once execution is claimed.

evidence: Confirmed the signature and replay arguments enumerate primitive, key, serializer, profile, verifier, and ledger assumptions and explicitly exclude intent, custody, permission, confidentiality, and business uniqueness.
Confirmed the executable HMAC is labeled educational and production implementations are directed to maintained cryptographic/protocol libraries.
Confirmed standards claims, application-profile policy, implementation mechanisms, and operational verification obligations remain distinct.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter never elevates a valid digest/signature, TLS, DPoP, nonce, timestamp, idempotency key, presigned URL, or passing snippet into a universal proof.

evidence: Snippet report artifacts/snippets/API-049/report.json records one passing deterministic local signing/replay state model with five exact outcomes.

Real RFC libraries/test vectors, proxy/CDN/mesh transforms, DPoP/token server, distributed nonce store, clocks, queues, streaming/trailers, key service/rotation, retries/idempotency, fault injection, and attack tests are future evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production signer/verifier, key custody system, distributed ledger, OAuth deployment, webhook provider, or presigned capability was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed primitive guarantees, RFC 9421 profile coverage, RFC 9530 digest binding, semantic/proxy canonicalization, time plus distributed nonce state, DPoP's exact scope, proof versus business duplication, key/algorithm lifecycle, presigned capabilities, safe verification ordering, observability, and tests as one coherent layered model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through maintained profile libraries, trusted effective-target boundaries, raw bounded content hashing, algorithm/key/profile registry, skew/age policy, authenticate-then-atomic nonce reservation, regional failure policy, fresh signed retry plus stable operation key, rotation overlap, generic errors, safe telemetry, SDK vectors, captured production-like proxy requests, concurrency/fault tests, and resource quotas. Concrete profile parameters remain threat- and topology-specific.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module begins by separating guarantees, derives component/digest/canonicalization/freshness requirements, then connects DPoP, idempotency, key lifecycle, presigned URLs, operations, and evidence. Ten examples cover distinct coverage, digest, time, distributed, retry, proxy, DPoP, webhook, rotation, and DoS cases; five exercises culminate in offline industrial-device transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
